title: Orders and service deteriorating at Northwind Pharma Distributors (Fictional) 4821
silent_period_basis: Days from estimated onset until a weekly manual review of order totals would flag it (assumption: flags a >25% month-on-month drop).

evidence.label: Fill rate
evidence.caption: Share of what the customer asked for that we actually shipped. Falling fill rate usually means a supply problem on our side, not a demand problem on theirs.
evidence.definition: sum(qty_filled)/sum(qty_ordered), last 4 weeks. Compared to baseline fill rate.
evidence.note: Fill rate on SKU-CKD-01 for this account, last 4 weeks

evidence.label: Order volume
evidence.caption: How much less (or more) this account bought recently than its own normal. A drop alone is weak; a drop with other signals is a pattern.
evidence.definition: Units ordered, last 4 weeks vs baseline weekly mean x 4, as fractional change.

evidence.label: Stock cover
evidence.caption: How many days of this product the warehouse can still ship. Under about a week it becomes the likely cause of downstream customer problems.
evidence.definition: warehouse on_hand / trailing 4-week mean daily dispatch, per SKU.

evidence.label: Order value
evidence.caption: Same idea as volume but in rupees, so a mix shift to cheaper products shows up.
evidence.definition: Order value (INR), same windows as order_volume_delta.

evidence.label: Complaints
evidence.caption: How many more complaints this account raised than it normally does in four weeks. Note that fewer orders with more complaints means the experience got worse, not just busier.
evidence.definition: Count of complaints (kinds: service, delivery, billing) in the last 4 weeks vs baseline. COUNT, not rate: this is what deck slide 7 shows ('Complaints up 47%').

evidence.label: Delivery delay
evidence.caption: Average lateness against what we promised. Customers feel this before they complain.
evidence.definition: Mean (delivered_date - promised_date) in days, last 4 weeks.

evidence.label: Touchpoints
evidence.caption: How much less we are in touch with this account. Relationships fade quietly before orders fall.
evidence.definition: Visits+calls+WhatsApp touchpoints per 4 weeks vs baseline.

evidence.label: Supplier ETA slips
evidence.caption: Each slip of the supplier's promised arrival date is evidence of a supplier or manufacturing delay.
evidence.definition: Number of times inbound_eta has moved later in the last 28 days.

evidence.label: Response time
evidence.caption: How much slower we are answering this account. Slow replies make a supply problem feel like neglect.
evidence.definition: Median (first_response_at - opened_at), last 4 weeks vs baseline.

steps.summary: Incident INC-2026-0001: critical, risk 100, 4 source systems (crm, inventory, orders, support).
Ranked 2 candidate cause(s) from the fixed taxonomy; top: supplier_delay (confidence 0.794).
Retrieved 5 similar records with TF-IDF; best INC-017 (similarity 0.603).
Drafted a 7-step plan from SOP-01 and INC-017; requires Operations Manager.

conditions.text: Stock cover under 7 days on an SKU this account buys
Supplier ETA slipped at least once
Fill rate fell on that SKU
Visit gap, rep coverage or touchpoint drop

memory_matches.title: Stockist orders fell after CKD-MBD binder supplier slip
memory_matches.resolution: Reallocate inventory from lower-priority accounts, escalate supplier, contact customer

memory_matches.title: Nephrology clinic orders paused during iron supplement supplier delay
memory_matches.resolution: Escalate supplier, contact clinic with revised ETA, partial reallocation from regional buffer

memory_matches.title: Chemist chain switched source during prolonged supplier delay
memory_matches.resolution: Late outreach after stock returned; no interim supply offered

memory_matches.title: Hospital pharmacy short-shipped after phosphate binder supplier slip
memory_matches.resolution: Split remaining stock across hospital accounts pro rata, escalate supplier, share revised ETA with pharmacy

memory_matches.title: Chemist chain outlets out of stock after central DC transfer delay
memory_matches.resolution: Temporary direct dispatch to affected outlets, coordinate with chain logistics

narrative.text: Sentinel found 4 independent source systems moving together: Order volume -31% vs this account's own normal; Order value -41% vs this account's own normal; Complaints +48% vs this account's own normal; Delivery delay 1.5 days vs 0.4 days normally.
Stock cover under 7 days on an SKU this account buys: Stock cover for SKU-CKD-01 at 2.2 days vs a normal of 33 days.
Supplier ETA slipped at least once: Supplier ETA slips: the inbound date for SKU-CKD-01 moved 2 times in 28 days.
Fill rate fell on that SKU: Fill rate 62% vs a normal of 98%.
Deliveries later than promised: Delivery delay 1.5 days vs 0.4 days normally.
The cause rule that fits best is supplier delay; the customer-side symptoms follow from it rather than from a demand change.

Organizational memory's closest match is INC-017 (Stockist orders fell after CKD-MBD binder supplier slip), resolved by: Reallocate inventory from lower-priority accounts, escalate supplier, contact customer.

Contact the account to understand the cause of delay
Propose a payment plan with a reduced credit limit
Decide on payment plan or credit hold
Apply the decided order release rule in operations
Escalate overdue balance to finance and business head
Place the account on credit hold
Negotiate recovery of the overdue balance
